cases.name: adds-a-csv-to-table-skill
cases.promptMarkdown:
Add a new skill to this repository called csv-to-table that converts a CSV file into a
GitHub-flavored markdown table. Put the conversion logic in
skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs with its test at
skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.test.mjs, and an eval case at
evals/csv-to-table/converts-a-simple-csv/ (including graders/skill-fired.md as the tool-use
indicator, plus at least one grader that scores the outcome). Follow this repository's own
practice for adding a skill end to end, and stop once the repository's gate command named in
CLAUDE.md passes. End with a short final message listing every file you created.

graders.name: script-test-quality
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is the test file for a script that converts CSV text into a GitHub-flavored markdown table.
Score 1 only if the file imports the conversion function from its sibling script (a relative
import of ./convert.mjs or similar) and contains at least one real assertion that exercises the
conversion — for example checking that a header row and a separator row appear, or that a comma
in the input becomes a column boundary in the output. Score 0 if the file is empty, contains no
assertions, never imports the script it claims to test, or only asserts something trivial that
would pass for any implementation (like "the function exists").

graders.graderMarkdown:
This is a newly authored SKILL.md for a skill named csv-to-table. Score 1 only if ALL five
criteria hold; quote the number of any criterion that fails.

2. Frontmatter `description` is third person and names a concrete trigger a user would type
   (converting a CSV, producing a markdown table, or similar).
3. The frontmatter contains no `<` or `>` characters.
4. The body is an instruction sheet, judged at the section level: it has (a) at most two
   sentences of prose before its first list, (b) a numbered list of steps in which every item

   "how it works" explanation. Such material belongs in a references/ file.
5. The whole file is under 80 lines.

name: csv-to-table
description: Converts a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. Use when the user asks to convert a CSV to a markdown table, turn CSV data into a table, render a CSV as GFM, or paste CSV data and wants it as a markdown table.
---

# CSV to table

Convert a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table.

## Steps

1. Run `node <skill>/scripts/convert.mjs <path-to-csv>` to print the GFM markdown table for that
   file to stdout. Pass CSV text on stdin instead of a path when the data has not been saved to a
   file yet (`cat data.csv | node <skill>/scripts/convert.mjs`).
2. Put the printed table wherever the user asked for it: inline in your reply, or written to the
   file they named.

## When not to use

- The input is not valid CSV (already JSON, TSV, or another delimited format) — convert it to CSV
  first, or ask the user for CSV.
- The request needs computed columns, filtering, sorting, or aggregation, not a literal
  CSV-to-table conversion — do that transformation first, then convert the result with this skill.

# CSV to table

Converts a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table.

## Steps

1. Locate the CSV file the user means; ask for a path if none is given or more than one CSV file
   matches.
2. Run `node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs <csv-path>` to print the converted table.
3. Save the output to a markdown file next to the input, using the same basename with a `.md`
   extension (e.g. `data.csv` becomes `data.md`), unless the user names a different destination.
   Pass that path as a second argument to the script to have it write the file directly:
   `node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs <csv-path> <output-path>`.
4. Report the output path and show the table's first few rows so the user can confirm it looks
   right.

## When not to use

- The input is not CSV (already tab-separated, JSON, or an Excel file) — convert it to CSV first.
- The user wants a different output format (HTML table, CSV cleanup only, etc.) rather than a
  GitHub-flavored markdown table.

graders.evidence:
--- name: csv-to-table description: Converts a CSV file (or raw CSV text) into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. Use whenever the user provides CSV data, a .csv file, or spreadsheet-style rows and columns and wants it rendered as a markdown table for docs, PRs, issues, or chat. --- # csv-to-table Converts CSV input into a GitHub-flavored markdown (GFM) table. ## Usage Run the conversion script with a path to a CSV file: node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs path/to/data.csv Or pipe CSV text on stdin: cat data.csv | node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs The script prints a GFM table to stdout: a header row taken from the first CSV row, a `---` separator row, and one row per remaining CSV record. ## Notes - Fields are parsed per RFC 4180: values containing commas, quotes, or newlines must be wrapped in double quotes, and `""` inside a quoted field is an escaped quote. - Pipe characters (`|`) and backslashes in cell values are escaped so the output renders as a single valid table, and embedded newlines are converted to `
` so a cell never breaks across table rows. - The first row is always treated as the header row.

--- name: csv-to-table description: Converts a CSV file into a GitHub-flavored markdown table. Use this whenever the user wants CSV data (a file path or pasted CSV text) turned into, previewed as, or embedded as a markdown table. --- # CSV to table Converts CSV data into a GitHub-flavored markdown (GFM) table using `scripts/convert.mjs`. ## Instructions 1. Get the CSV onto disk if it isn't already (e.g. write pasted CSV text to a temp file). 2. Run the script, passing the path to the CSV file: ``` node skills/csv-to-table/scripts/convert.mjs ``` 3. The script prints the finished GFM table to stdout. Paste that directly into your response — do not hand-convert the CSV yourself. ## Notes - The first row of the CSV is treated as the table header. - Quoted fields (including ones containing commas, escaped `""` quotes, or embedded newlines) are parsed correctly. - Literal `|` characters in a cell are escaped as `\|` so the table still renders correctly. Embedded newlines in a cell are rendered as `
`. - An empty CSV file produces empty output.
